thread:
maya: Seeing a sharp uptick in outbound failures from model-pull workers in us-west-2. Errors look like repeated connection resets and 'connect: cannot assign requested address' from the downloader.

sam: yeah noticed retries spiking in the job logs around 18:32 UTC, lots of TIME_WAIT on the nodes.

liam: can you paste a small log snippet? suspect ephemeral port exhaustion hitting the NAT.

maya: paste_logs:
```
2026-03-18T18:31:45Z downloader[pid=4321]: fetch model failed: connect: cannot assign requested address
2026-03-18T18:31:46Z downloader[pid=4325]: HTTP GET https://models.internal.redwood/model-abc.tar -> ECONNRESET
2026-03-18T18:31:47Z kernel: [net] node-xx TIME_WAIT: 18432
```

ekaterina: confirmed from host metrics: ephemeral port usage trending to 64k on several NAT IPs. NAT gateway is showing port allocation saturated for the AZ.

sam: are these workers using short-lived connections per shard? I recall the downloader opens new TCP per file chunk.

maya: yes, downloads spawn 20 parallel clients per pod and we do sharding per chunk. No long-lived pooling.

liam: immediate mitigations: 1) add an extra NAT gateway in the affected AZs (fast but costs $) 2) enable S3 VPC endpoint where possible 3) put an egress proxy (envoy/squid) to multiplex connections and reuse sockets to model storage.

ekaterina: +1 to egress proxy — gives connection pooling and HTTP/2 multiplexing. We have a tested envoy chart.

maya: can we flip S3 endpoint quickly for model storage? some models still live on internal object store behind public IPs so not all traffic goes to S3.

sam: for public endpoints, egress proxy helps. Also we should change downloader to use persistent HTTP/1.1 keep-alive or HTTP/2 and reuse connections. Short-term patch: reduce per-pod parallel clients from 20 -> 6.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1423 NAT-port-exhaustion-us-west-2 (link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-1423)

liam: operational playbook notes:
- deploy 1 extra NAT GW in each AZ with route table update (manual, ~5-10m)
- create regional ALB + egress-proxy ASG in each AZ for model pulls (can roll quickly via k8s)
- configure iptables conntrack tuning on proxy hosts (increase hashsize if needed)
- update downloader to use connection pooling (PR queued)

maya: cost question — extra NAT gateways will add $$$. What's rough delta for adding 3 NATs?

ekaterina: estimate: NAT GW ~$0.045/hour + data processing fees; in outage mode 3 NATs across AZs ~ $10-20k/month depending on traffic. Egress proxy instances cheaper but ops overhead.

sam: long-term: consider deploying a regional egress fleet (pooling across AZs) + TCP connection reuse lib in the downloader. Also investigate AWS NAT Gateway port expansion per ENI (we already use multiple EIPs?)

liam: quick checks to run on affected node: 
```
ss -s | grep TIME_WAIT
netstat -anp | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
curl -v https://models.internal.redwood/health || true
```

maya: doing those now, will reduce parallelism and spin up a small envoy replica set in us-west-2. Will post updates.

oncall-bot: @maya assigned as incident lead for INC-2026-1423

maya: update 18:52 UTC — reduced downloader parallelism; TIME_WAIT counts falling, errors reduced. Envoy proxies deployed (3 replicas per AZ) and routing model pulls through proxy. Initial metrics show 70% drop in new outbound connections to NAT IPs.

ekaterina: great. next steps: schedule follow-up to instrument connection reuse metrics, add test workload to validate proxy at scale, and plan a runbook entry for future port-surge events.

liam: also create a checklist for pre-warming additional NAT IPs and for when to switch to VPC endpoints / proxy.

sam: I'll open the downloader PR to enable HTTP/2 + keepalive by default and add a configurable concurrency cap.

maya: thanks all — keeping this thread for post-incident notes and runbook entries. :thumbsup:
